newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas rises with temporary weekend heat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas rises with temporary weekend heat.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices gained additional ground Friday as lingering heat in the South and Northeast kept buyers in the marketplace, industry sources said.
Swing prices on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes edged three to four cents higher into the low-to-mid $1.70s per million British thermal units despite the normal drop in weekend demand.
At the Henry Hub, La., gas traded as high as $1.77 shortly before nomination deadlines.
Prices were similarly stronger in the Appalachian region where traders reported closing most swing deals in the high-$1.80s to low-$1.90s.
In the Permian basin, prices were mostly steady in the $1.47-1.51 area despite expectations for softer prices ahead of the weekend.
The margin between Permian and Waha failed to budge as deals were done at the western hub in the high-$1.50s to about $1.60. On Transwestern, gas sold in the high-$1.40s to about $1.50.

In the Midcontinent, where temperatures were a few degrees above-normal, prices gained a couple of cents to the high-$1.50s to low-$1.60s. There was a scramble for gas late, which pushed prices to as high as $1.63.

Many traders thought the recent uptick in cash prices in the Gulf and Midcontinent markets would be short-lived as forecasters called for below-normal temperatures next week in many parts of the U.S., including the Gulf Coast.
